direction.name: The split stage
direction.idea: Half the screen never moves. One side is a fixed photograph (or object, or product view) that stays in place for the whole visit; the other side is a calm scrolling column with everything you need to read. The fixed half keeps the feeling present while the reader gets on with the facts, like sitting in the room while reading the menu. As sections pass, the fixed image may quietly change to the one that matches.
direction.composition: Desktop: a two-column page, 50/50 or 45/55. One column is `position: sticky; top: 0; height: 100svh` and holds a single photograph filling it edge to edge, or the object centred on a flat field. The other column scrolls and holds all content in a single narrow measure (max 46ch) with comfortable padding (48–72px): name and one-line description first, then sections separated by generous space, then contact and footer. Headings in the scrolling column are modest (32–44px). The column grounds differ: photograph on one side, flat paper colour on the other, meeting at a clean vertical edge. On a phone the fixed half becomes a 60svh image at the top that stays sticky behind the first section, then releases.
direction.typography: A text-first setting: a readable serif or a calm sans at 17–19px, with one display size for the name. Left-aligned throughout.
direction.colour: The paper colour of the reading column is chosen against the photograph: a tone taken from its shadows or its lightest area. One ink, optionally one accent ink for links and the action.
direction.imagery: One excellent portrait-orientation photograph for the fixed half, plus three or four more that crossfade in as their sections arrive. Small inline photographs in the reading column are optional and should be few.
direction.richness: A full-height photograph always in view, against a quiet, well-set column of text.
direction.pitfalls: The reading column must be genuinely well typeset, since it is half the page. Do not put cards or grids in it. Check that the fixed image crops well at short viewport heights. In blind tests the commonest complaint was monotony: several screens of the same split with only the text changing. Change what the reading half holds from section to section (a list, a large figure, a table, a full-colour panel, a drawing) and let at least one section break the split and run full width.

hero.name: Striped card beside the room
hero.blueprint: The viewport is split 50/50 with a 12px gap and 12px outer margins. The right half is one full-height photograph of the room, corners radiused 16px, `position: sticky` so it stays in view while the left half scrolls. The left half is a printed card: a flat paper-colour panel with the same 16px radius, and the subject's stripe (from its awning, label or ribbon) as the only ornament. Across the card's top runs a band 56px tall made of alternating bars of the single ink colour and paper, each bar 28px wide, built as a flex row of filled blocks. The same stripe returns as an 8px band above the footer and inside the button on hover. Under the band, centred: the wordmark about 300px wide, then a two-line headline in a light serif at clamp(40px, 3.6vw, 56px) in the ink colour, one supporting sentence at 17px held to 36ch, and the single action as a solid rectangular button. Three text links sit in one centred row at 15px, 28px above the card's bottom edge. One ink on paper; the photograph supplies every other colour.
hero.mobile: The photograph comes first at full width inside 12px margins, 48svh tall, with the 16px radius. The card follows and overlaps the photograph's bottom edge by 24px using a negative margin. Its striped band is 40px tall; below it the wordmark at 56% width, the headline at 8vw on two lines, the sentence and the button, all centred. The links wrap into the card's foot.
hero.headline: A warm two-line welcome of three to six words, up to about 18 characters per line at 3.6vw.

type.note: A contemporary slab with smooth curves and unbracketed serifs, even enough to carry headings and paragraphs alike. Suits developer tools, personal sites, open-source and nonprofit projects.

palette.name: Bone, green, chocolate
palette.note: Bone ground with chocolate-brown text takes most of the page. The green is spent on one large flat block, about a third of a screen, and on the button; all other colour comes from photographs.

photos.title: Fog and quiet
photos.note: misty, muted, minimal landscapes and empty horizons; calm areas for text

motion.name: Slow crossfade
motion.description: The principal photograph quietly changes: three or four images of the same framing crossfade over about 1.6 seconds, holding five to six seconds each, or the fixed image changes when its matching section arrives. It should feel like light shifting in a room. Pause when the tab is hidden; under reduced motion show only the first image.

sections.name: Narrow column, empty field
sections.blueprint: A single text column 300–340px wide, its left edge at 15% of the viewport width, starting 64px below the section top. It holds four or five short paragraphs at 15–16px with leading 1.5 and one blank line between them; the first paragraph is in medium weight and full ink, the rest in regular weight and the soft ink. No heading, no image, no button; one underlined text link may end the last paragraph. The remaining three-quarters of the 1440 screen is untouched ground, and the section is only as tall as the text plus 160px of padding below. The column's left edge must match a line used elsewhere on the page (the wordmark's left edge or a later column). Where the page has a large object or a fixed photograph, this column is the small text beside it. Holds 90–150 words comfortably.
sections.mobile: The column becomes 78% of the width, left-aligned at the 20px margin, so a strip of empty ground remains on the right as a deliberate margin. Text stays at 15–16px with the first paragraph in medium weight. Padding is 72px above and 96px below.

sections.name: Pinned heading, passing rows
sections.blueprint: One flat saturated field, full-bleed, as tall as its content. Columns 1–5: the heading, two or three words, at clamp(56px, 6.6vw, 104px) in the heaviest weight, position: sticky; top: 32px, so it holds while the right side travels. Columns 7–12: four to six capability blocks stacked with 120px between them. Each block is a title at 28px bold, then a two-part row: a portrait photograph at 3:4, 180–220px wide with square corners, and beside it, top-aligned, a plain list of four to six short lines at 18px with 14px between lines. Photographs alternate between the left and the right of their list, so the column does not read as a ladder. One ink colour, chosen for contrast on the field. The heading releases when the bottom of the last block reaches it.
sections.mobile: The heading becomes a sticky bar at the top of the section: one line at 9vw on the field colour with 12px padding, holding while blocks pass under it. Each block stacks its title, a full-width 4:3 photograph, then the list at 17px. 72px between blocks.

sections.name: Itinerary on a slip
sections.blueprint: The process is printed as an itinerary or receipt. One paper-coloured slip 420–480px wide stands on a contrasting flat ground at columns 7–11; its bottom edge is a zigzag cut with clip-path and its top edge is straight. The heading, two to four words at clamp(40px, 4.4vw, 68px), sits in columns 1–5 with a 30ch paragraph, top-aligned with the slip. On the slip, in the text face at 16px with tabular figures: stages grouped under time headings that carry the order ('Monday', 'Midweek', 'Friday'), each heading in bold with 28px above it. Under a heading, two to four rows; each row has what happens on the left, a duration or time on the right, and a leader of round 4px dots between. The final row is inverted, paper-coloured text on a full-width ink bar 44px tall, and states the result: what the reader holds at the end and the total time.
sections.mobile: The heading and paragraph come first. The slip follows at full width minus 16px margins, keeping its zigzag bottom edge. Rows keep left text, dots and right value on one line; long descriptions wrap under the left text. The inverted final row stays full width.

sections.name: Portrait and offset quotation
sections.blueprint: A 12-column row on the page ground with wide margins. A portrait of the speaker, 3:4, fills columns 2–5 and is tall, about 70svh; it takes whatever mask the page gives its photographs (square corners, or the page's one motif shape). The quotation occupies columns 7–12 and starts 120px lower than the top of the portrait: four to six lines at clamp(26px, 2.6vw, 40px) in a light or regular weight, leading 1.2, measure about 26ch. The name and role sit 32px beneath the quotation at 16px, on its left edge. A second, small photograph (1:1, columns 10–11) hangs 96px below the attribution and shows the place or the thing the speaker is talking about. There is no heading. Nothing is centred; every edge lands on a column line, and the two vertical offsets are the design.
sections.mobile: The portrait runs at 72% width from the left margin, 3:4. The quotation follows at 24px, full width, starting 32px beneath. Name and role sit under it. The small second photograph sits at 44% width against the right margin, 48px lower, overlapping nothing.

sections.name: Answers as reading text
sections.blueprint: The questions and answers are set as continuous reading text, like the notes at the back of a programme. A heading of two or three words at 28–32px sits in columns 1–3, top-aligned. Columns 5–12 hold the text in two columns (`columns: 2; column-gap: 56px`), each about 36ch wide, at 16–17px with leading 1.55. Each item is one paragraph: the question is the opening run-in, set in the medium weight in the full ink and ending with its question mark, and the answer continues on the same line in the regular weight. Paragraphs are separated by 20px and carry `break-inside: avoid` so none splits across columns. No toggles, no icons, no boxes. Eight to fourteen items fit on one screen, which is the point: everything is answered at a glance. Where the page's reading column is narrow, use one column.
sections.mobile: One column at 16px with 20px margins. The heading leads at 24px. Each paragraph keeps its run-in question in the medium weight, with 18px between paragraphs. The section may run to two screens; do not collapse it into an accordion.

sections.name: A plain sentence, one action
sections.blueprint: The page ends on an almost empty screen. On the page ground, with no band and no panel, one sentence of eight to fourteen words is set at 18–22px in the regular weight, in the full ink, no wider than 34ch, on the same left edge as the page's text column (or centred only if the whole page is centred). 24px beneath it sits one small filled button, about 40px tall with 18px side padding, and optionally one text link beside it on the same baseline. That is all. Above the sentence leave at least 30svh of empty ground and below it at least 20svh before the footer line, so the emptiness reads as decided. The sentence is written as something a person would say, and it names the action plainly. No headline-sized type appears anywhere in this section.
sections.mobile: Identical in spirit: the sentence at 18px with 20px margins, the button beneath at its natural width (not full width), 44px tall. Keep 20svh of empty ground above the sentence and 14svh below the button, before the footer line.

sections.name: A single quiet line
sections.blueprint: No footer block at all. After at least 30svh of empty page ground, one baseline 30px above the bottom edge carries three items in the page's ordinary small text size (14–16px), the same size and weight as the navigation: at the left margin, what this is in three or four words; centred, two to five links separated by 24px of space; at the right margin, the year and a privacy link. Use a three-column grid (1fr auto 1fr) so the centre group is truly centred whatever the side lengths. No logo, no background change, no line above it, no columns. Links are in the full ink; the rest in the softer ink. If the page has a narrow text column, the three items may instead sit on that column's left edge as one wrapped line. The restraint only works if the page above has already made its invitation.
sections.mobile: Three short lines at 14px on the left margin with 8px between them: the description, the links on one wrapped line, then year and privacy. Links stay in the full ink. Leave 20svh of empty ground above and 24px below.

references.name: Flowjam
references.idea: A persistent frosted sidebar card holds the pitch and buttons while a soft-serif content column scrolls past it; beyond that there is no idea stronger than proof by logos and videos.
references.hero: Grainy off-white page. A tall rounded card about 26% of the viewport wide is pinned at the left and runs off the bottom; frosted over blurred pink and yellow flowers, it holds the logo, a two-line serif tagline, a short blurb and two pill buttons in hot pink and charcoal. The main column starts 32% from the left: a hot-pink pill badge, a three-line serif headline at 4.2vw, then a paragraph whose first sentence is grey and the rest black. A lone charcoal pill button floats far right at mid-height. Below: a heart icon with a proof line, then the top of a four-column logo grid with dotted borders.
references.type: Gelica throughout: a soft, slightly bulbous serif at regular weight, 60px headline with tight -0.05em tracking, 16 to 19px body, down to about 9px in the sidebar. One family for everything including buttons keeps the tone warm but flattens the difference between labels and prose.
references.colour: #f8f8f6 #e7e8e4 #1c0f1f #ff4fe0 #0c0c0c #7b3ff2 — Warm paper white with grain, near-black aubergine text and one hot-pink accent used for the badge and primary button; a purple heart appears once. The footer flips to black.
references.imagery: Rounded-corner video thumbnails of founders talking to camera and product UI clips, each with a small round play button bottom-left; monochrome client logos in a dotted-line grid; blurred floral blobs behind the frosted sidebar.
references.layout: A fixed 26% sidebar card at left for the whole scroll; content occupies one column to its right, split into two for video tiles and four for logos. Sections are separated by whitespace only. The footer is a rounded black panel that still leaves the sidebar in place.

sections.description: Four-column grid of client logos drawn with faint dotted cell borders, each cell roughly 240px wide and 115px tall with the logo centred in dark grey monochrome. Sixteen or more logos over four rows, no captions. Above it, a centred line with a purple heart glyph and a sentence whose first word is black and the rest grey serves as the heading.

Two-column grid of video cards. Each card has a header row with the client name in 14px serif and a one-line result in tiny grey beneath it at left, and a small outlined pill link at right; then a 16:9 thumbnail with about 10px radius and a round play button over its bottom-left corner. Cards are divided by hairlines rather than boxes, and some thumbnails are flat type frames instead of photos.

A rounded black panel inset from the page edges, sitting right of the sidebar. Its background is a short phrase repeated in dark-grey serif at about 5vw, rows offset so the words tile like wallpaper. Centred over it: a two-line white serif headline at about 2.5vw and a small stat line. The lower third holds the logo at left and four narrow columns of tiny text.

steal: Pin a narrow card with logo, one-line pitch and both actions beside the scrolling content, so the call to action never leaves the screen and no top nav is needed.
Set one sentence of a paragraph in grey and the rest in black to rank two claims without changing size or weight.
Tile a short phrase as dark-on-black wallpaper behind the footer headline.

references.name: Le Petit Bleu
references.idea: The cafe's teal-and-white stripes become the whole system: one teal ink on cream, everything boxed in thin double outlines like printed menu cards, beside a permanently visible photo of the room.
references.hero: Viewport split 50/50 with 12px gaps. Left: a cream panel with a thin pale-teal outline and rounded corners. Inside, a second outlined box is the nav bar: two-line hamburger left, teal brush-script logo about 300px wide centred, a caps order link right. Below, a two-line light serif headline at about 3.5vw, centred, in teal, then two centred stacks, each a bold caps label, a serif line and a solid teal button wrapped in a second thin outline. Right: a full-height rounded photo of a striped booth, with an outlined hours bar across its top, three slide dots bottom-left and a white address card bottom-right.
references.type: Self Modern, a light bookish serif, for headline and 15px body; Matter SQ bold caps for labels and buttons; Archive Mono Pro typewriter caps for menu rows; a brush-script logo. Section titles are tall condensed serif caps sized so four to seven letters fill the column.
references.colour: #fcfbf7 #13a7b2 #058599 #cfe5e7 #e9b81f — Cream paper and a single teal used for every word, rule, outline and button; no black anywhere. Yellow, floral reds and marble enter only through the interior photographs.
references.imagery: Bright, saturated interior and food photographs; the right-hand panel is a full-height slideshow with rounded corners. Small food shots sit in a horizontal strip, and a fine line drawing of the shopfront with one teal awning fills a card.
references.layout: The left half scrolls as a stack of outlined cream cards (full-width or two-up) with 12px gaps while the right half stays fixed. Card contents are centred. A sticky nav card rides over the stack. On mobile the photo becomes the hero card's background.

sections.description: A card containing only the section word in tall condensed serif caps, teal, sized so its four letters fill the column edge to edge. Below it, a stack of full-width outlined rows about 36px high, each with a category name in typewriter mono caps at left and a thin plus sign at right, separated by 6px gaps. Above the title: a ticker row of tiny caps and a strip of four small food photos with rounded corners.

The same giant condensed title treatment, then centred serif paragraphs in teal with underlined links in a narrow measure of about 280px. Further down, a landscape photo of the two proprietors with a centred two-line caption in tiny sans, followed by more centred paragraphs. All of it lives in the left half while the right photo panel has advanced to a shelf-wall image.

A header row with a tiny bold caps label at left and a script follow-us link with arrow at right, then three portrait images (about 3:5) with 12px rounded corners in a row, the third cropped by the column edge to imply a carousel. Directly below, the next giant section title begins and is cropped by the viewport.

steal: Print everything in one brand ink on cream, including body text, rules and buttons, and let photographs supply the other colours.
Wrap buttons and panels in a second thin outline offset by a few pixels to get a printed-ticket feel.
Keep a tall photo panel fixed on one half and scroll a stack of cards on the other, swapping the photo as sections change.

references.name: Odyssée
references.idea: A medical-aesthetics clinic presented like a skincare editorial: soft-lit close-ups of skin and slow muted loops carry the page, a thin navy serif voice argues for method over myth, and the page ends on a rolling pearl engraved with the wordmark, one polished object that stands for the result.
references.hero: A full-bleed muted video portrait (a woman resting her chin on her hands in pale grey-blue studio light) fills the screen, followed at once by a second full-bleed close-up of lips and jaw. No headline: a single 42px strip crosses the exact vertical middle in white, the serif wordmark at x=20, an 18px serif tagline about medical aesthetics at column 3 (x≈255), and four tiny tracked caps links on the right ending in the booking link, which all but vanishes against the pale picture. The strip holds while both pictures pass under it, then becomes a sticky 42px header. The entrance is a flat warm grey veil carrying only the wordmark and tagline, lifting over about 2.5s.
references.type: Two families. psTimes, a condensed Times-style serif at weight 350, for statements at 48px (3.3vw) and 32px and for titles and the tagline at 18px, sentence case, leading about 1.0-1.05, every statement with a first-line indent of one column. Basel Grotesk at 430 for 14px body and 12px lightly tracked uppercase labels and links; the house version sets those in sentence case at 16px. Fixed px sizes per breakpoint, no clamp().
references.colour: #fffcf8 #1e305e #ffffff #28292a — A warm cream ground behind nearly everything, one deep navy for 88% of the text, the progress rule and a duotone on secondary pictures, white only over photographs. A single small red dot on a live clock is the only accent; the photographs supply skin tones, pale grey-blue studio grounds and a champagne pearl.
references.imagery: Soft, even studio light on pale grey-blue backgrounds, natural skin with no retouching gloss, tight crops (lips, eye, nostril, knees) and one face turned 90 degrees for tension; slow, nearly still muted loops of skin, serum drops and bubbles used as living photographs; a navy duotone on two link cards. Square corners and cover crops everywhere.
references.layout: 20px outer margins on a 12-column grid (columns about 117px). Text has two anchors: column 3 (x≈255) for statements, body and labels, and the exact centre line for right-half paragraphs and cards. Media is always full-bleed, an exact half (720/720) or flush tiles with no gutter. Cream gaps of 232-552px separate sections, roughly one idea per screen; the closing contacts huddle in the left half.

sections.description: A 48px light serif statement on three lines from column 3 to the right margin with a one-column first-line indent, a small 108x161 double-portrait thumbnail docked at the left margin, then 14px body in a narrow column and a booking link.

Pinned for four steps: a counter, a label and a 1400px rule whose navy fill grows a quarter per step, over four 350x263 muted 5s video tiles flush edge to edge; the active tile at full strength, the other three washed to about 10%, each with an 18px serif title beneath.

Split on the centre line: a tall 672x1233 muted skin close-up holds the right half while scrolling, a small 233x291 clip of a serum drop sits just left of centre with a short caption, and a three-word 48px serif headline arrives at x=20 at mid-height.

Contact rows, an opening-hours table where only today is in full navy, and a live local clock with a pulsing dot; then the page lifts away to reveal a fixed full-bleed 9s loop of a pearl rolling on a pale grey surface with the wordmark engraved round it.

steal: Make video behave like photographs: muted, looping, with posters, 5-29s of nearly still subjects started by script when they come into view, square corners and cover crops everywhere.

Give every serif statement a first-line indent of exactly one grid column and anchor the block at column 3 with 20px outer margins, so the indent reads as a deliberate grid step; use the exact centre line as the second anchor for half-width pictures and right-half paragraphs.

End on real local detail (an hours table that marks today, a live local clock), then reveal a fixed full-bleed brand object as the last screen. The site's tiny white caps nav over pale skin all but disappears; the house version is a plain bar with the booking action as a real button.
references.media: Video is the main medium: a 27s portrait loop and a second close-up fill the first screen, then four 5s tiles flush edge to edge, a 720/720 diptych, a tall half-width clip held while scrolling, a full-bleed band that fades up from cream, two navy duotone cards, and a fixed pearl loop revealed under the footer. Nine images and eight muted, looping videos with posters, started by script; no canvas.
references.motion: No preloader: a warm grey veil lifts off the hero video over about 2.5-3s with the type already in place. Under Lenis the features section pins for four steps, cross-fading tiles over 0.3s cubic-bezier(0.16,1,0.3,1) as the navy rule grows, images fade over 0.5s cubic-bezier(0,0,0.2,1), underlines grow by background-size over .4s expo-out and the page lifts off a fixed bottom layer to reveal the pearl, but content is opacity-gated, so mid-scroll frames show empty cream, and there is no reduced-motion rule.
